Subject: Thanks for downloading the Redwood Benchmark — quick demo?

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks for downloading our 2026 inference benchmark — I pulled your request from the download flow and wanted to see if you'd be open to a short demo to walk through the results and how Redwood could help Acme Analytics lower per-query cost while hitting your latency SLOs.

A few quick notes on the report:
- We include both streaming and batch throughput profiles for common sequence-length distributions.
- There's a cost-per-token sensitivity table for quantized vs FP16 deployments.
- We also highlight common prefix-caching opportunities for analytics-heavy workloads.

Would you be available for a 30-minute demo next week? A couple slots I have open:
- Tue Dec 1, 10:00 AM PST
- Tue Dec 1, 3:00 PM PST
- Wed Dec 2, 11:00 AM PST

I attached a 1-page summary of the benchmark in case that helps. If you'd prefer, I can loop in one of our AEs (Marissa) to run the session.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-summary.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Sales Development Representative
Redwood Inference

Hi Dylan (and Marissa),

Thanks — the summary was helpful. We'd definitely be interested in a demo to understand the tradeoffs around streaming latency vs batch throughput and how caching might impact our nightly analytics pipelines. Our CTO and platform lead will likely join. Possible times for us:
- Tue Dec 1, 10:00 AM PST (preferred)
- Tue Dec 1, 3:00 PM PST

If we need to move, Wed Dec 2 at 11:00 AM PST could also work.

A couple quick questions ahead of the call:
1) Can you cover model variants you recommend for 4–8k context analytics workloads?
2) Do you have any cost modeling for reserved vs burst capacity?

Attendees: Sanjay Rao, Liam Chen (Platform), Anika Gupta (Data Eng)

Thanks,
